## RO-1 — blocking: identity-conflicted lapse body still supplies resolved history

`decision_view.rs::lapse_history` lines96–122 filters raw entries by matching act/kind/referent/c0/comparable c1, without consulting the conflicting-record-ID set. Projection construction passes that accepted vector into `compare(..., !history.is_empty())` and exposes the identity in `lapseHistory`. Thus an observation with unresolvable conflicting identity can supply a resolved prior-lapse/restoration conclusion even though the reader diagnoses that same record identity globally as ambiguous.

Actual control at current frozen15d0: a unique A16 claim bound to current package bytes plus one valid recorded lapse gives `matches c0 again after observed lapse`, history `[rec:synthetic:lapse-a]`. Add a second schema-valid act_lapsed body with **the same recordId**, all facts equal except c1 equals c0 rather than changed: the view still reports exactly that resolved matches-again state/history. It emits global `ambiguous duplicate record identity: rec:synthetic:lapse-a` and rejects the second body as noncomparable, while accepting the first body under the unresolved identity. No sequence/schema read failure occurs. This is semantic identity-resolution leakage, not a HashMap overwrite and not a claim of native origin.

Required repair: carry observation identity resolution into per-contender and aggregate history derivation. Preserve both raw claims and their source/identity limits; a conflicted observation cannot supply a resolved lapse-history dependency merely because one body passes the comparable-change filter. Current file-byte equality remains an observable fact, while whether a qualifying prior lapse was established remains unresolved. Do not simply discard uncertainty and label not-lapsed/no-history, erase claims, or replace the valid unique-lapse oracle. A separate unambiguous qualifying observation may still independently warrant history, with conflicting observation limits retained.

Focused successor acceptance: valid lapse control unchanged; identical observation copies deduplicate with all sources; conflicting same-ID bodies in both filename/enumeration orders do not supply resolved restoration/history; unrelated IDs/referents/c0/c1 do not inherit; per-contender and agreeing-capture aggregate histories both respect resolution; unaffected valid claims/current byte observations remain readable. No writer/replay/act-admission changes are required to repair this read-only dependency.
